entities.summary:
Saint Pothinus was the first bishop of Lyon and the first bishop of Gaul, playing a pivotal role in the early Christianization of the region. He is first mentioned in a letter attributed to Irenaeus of Lyon, which was sent from the Christian communities of Lyon and Vienne to the Roman province of Asia.

Pothinus was instrumental in establishing the Church in Gaul, and his legacy continued to shape the region's religious and cultural landscape for centuries to come. His leadership and vision helped to foster a sense of community and cooperation among the Christian communities, which in turn contributed to the spread of Christianity throughout the region.

The impact of Pothinus' leadership can still be felt today, with many of the churches and cathedrals he established remaining an important part of the region's cultural heritage. His example of leadership and service has inspired countless generations of Christians and continues to be celebrated as a testament to the power of faith and commitment.

In the words of Irenaeus himself, 'He is the first bishop of the Church of God, and the father of the Church of Gaul.' (Irenaeus, Against Heresies, Book V, Chapter 1)
